review_notes: All three articles confirm the initial Thapathana school slope failure on Asar 16 (2023-07-01) and renewed damage at the same site AFTER Shrawan 22. They do not give an exact date or count for the later slide episode(s); assigning 2023-08-07 as the event date would misread “after”. Cannot safely build a complete dated split.

Report establishes a newly active Mahabhir, Annapurna-7 slope during the 2024 monsoon but says debris falls whenever it rains. It supplies no individual failure date or event boundary; Aug 11 is publication, not verified onset.

The available archived body is unrelated site furniture. Headline confirms plural Myagdi landslides with one death and five missing but gives no individual sites, failure dates, or attribution; July 30 is publication only.

Both syndication copies describe the same seven families displaced after Saturday-night rain in Talla Tenchong, but flood, cracks above the settlement and slides at other named schools are mixed. They do not date/delineate one physical Talla Tenchong slope failure separately from ongoing instability or identify exact dates of distinct school-site slides.

Helicopter account identifies a real slide about 500 m above Chokpu that cyclically dams and releases the Melamchi river, but does not establish whether the slope failed once or repeatedly as independent episodes or the precise slide date. The June 15 overnight FLOOD start is not proof of a June 15 or 16 initial failure.
